abstract_text: In the marine ecosystems the cartilaginous fishes represent the oldest and most ecologically diverse vertebrates filling the upper levels of aquatic food webs with possible top-down control on the midlevel consumers. Because of their K-selected life-history (e.g. slow growth, late attainment of sexual maturity, long life spans, low fecundity) these species are particularly vulnerable to the human activities, mainly to the overexploitation, and many of them are at risk of extinction. Although sharks and skates play a key role in the biological communities, the effects of their decline on the marine ecosystem, due mostly to fishing activity, are still poorly known. Considering data coming mainly by scientific surveys (e.g. MEDITS) carried out in the last thirty years, the authors provide information on the species diversity and fluctuations of abundance of the chondrichthyes caught on the soft bottoms of the north-western Ionian Sea, focusing the analysis on the species composition change and variable vulnerability and exposure to fishing of the different species. In this respect, recent acquisitions on the distribution and abundance of elasmobranches in sensitive habitats of the Ionian and South Adriatic Sea, such as cold-water coral habitats and canyons, are reported. Since these habitats, less accessible to fishing, can provide a natural refuge for these vulnerable species, large-scale connected protected areas can be a potential management option for the cartilaginous fish conservation.

abstract_text: Every year in Europe thousands of elasmobranchs die for fishing and many of them are caught for commercial and human consumption. There is no shame in saying that elasmobranchs can represent a small variation to the constant consumption of bony fish. Raja clavata is one of the most common species of elasmobranchs employed along Adriatic coasts for this use. For this research, 30 specimens of Raja clavata has been collected by trawl from December 2018 till March 2019. From each specimen we obtained biometric data and then we removed fillets. The samples have been processed to obtain fatty acids profiles. Fatty acids have been extracted using Bligh e Dyer (1959) method and gaschromatography has been employed for the determination of fatty acids profiles. The rays with the larger dimensions showed a greater concentration of polyunsaturated fatty acids than smaller ones. This relationship between concentration of fatty acids and dimensions of the rays can lay the groundwork for a responsible and higher quality fishing activity. In fact, from one hand fatty acids, in particular polyunsaturated, are essential for human health. From the other hand, since these acids are more present in bigger animals (that maybe have already reproduced more than once), it appears useful the promotion of selective fishing activities towards the dimensionality of rays. Since in our country there are no limits and few regulations for the elasmobranchs fishing, these two issues could be used as useful points for the development of a more sustainable future fishing.

abstract_text: For most people the word “shark” conjures images of terror and fear. As one of the greatest marine predators, sharks easily receive a reputation as killing machines; in reality, however, sharks have far more to fear from humans than humans do from sharks. Misconceptions, lack of knowledge and negative attitudes towards sharks act as barriers preventing actions required to tackle threats to shark populations, limiting the success of global shark conservation initiatives. Shark conservation would become more sustainable if public understanding of this predatory fish and an appreciation of its ecological significance could be promoted. To provide essential baseline data for planning of these educational efforts, this project investigated the perceptions of 9 to 11 years-old primary school student’s in Rende, CS, (South Italy) about sharks, and their understanding of ecological concepts and shark-related knowledge. The aim of this study was: 1- to investigate primary school students’ understanding of ecological concepts and their shark-related knowledge level and to explore their misconceptions about sharks; 2- to collect students’ perceptions or beliefs about this top predator before and after the presentation to observe if theese change; 3- to examine any correlations among students’ conceptual knowledge, perceptions and beliefs for sharks. Twelve question items were developed to assess students’ perceptions and conceptual understanding of sharks. We submitted the questionnaire to the students before and after a 30 minute long presentation about biology, behavior, relationship with human and conservation of sharks. The presentation has increased the knowledge about sharks in the primary school students. For the two specific questions about the risk of a shark attack and the danger of sharks, we found more right answers in the after-test than in the before-test. The submitted test after presentation showed more students with a new positive view on sharks. The findings indicate that these students lack sufficient knowledge and possess misconceptions about sharks and their ecological significance in the marine ecosystem.

abstract_text: Assessing the presence, abundance and population status of marine elasmobranchs of high conservation concern is challenging given the harmful effects of many traditional sampling techniques and the logistical difficulty of studying these generally elusive, highly mobile and low abundance taxa. In this context, we are developing a non-invasive environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding assay to improve detection of elasmobranch species from water samples, aiming at improving knowledge on them and ultimately to contribute to their conservation. The methodological workflow assesses eDNA metabarcoding efficiency in detecting species diversity, including validation of the method under controlled conditions prior to implementation in the field. For this purpose, method development and validation were carried out using water samples from the Lisbon Oceanarium, a closed system where species diversity and abundance is known, and field testing was performed in the Marine Protected Area of Arrábida, Portugal, where there is some previous knowledge on elasmobranch diversity. Several steps were performed to optimize both sampling and molecular analysis, including choosing filter pore size diameter, eDNA extraction methods and specificity and consistency of PCR amplification. Two mitochondrial gene regions were tested as molecular barcodes, namely the cytochrome oxidase subunit I (COI) and the NADH dehydrogenase subunit II (ND2), and checked for specificity to elasmobranch eDNA and taxonomic resolution. Nitrocelloluse membrane filters with 0.45 µm pore diameter performed best for water sample filtration coupled to Qiagen DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit for eDNA extraction. The eDNA metabarcoding assay for ND2 proved highly specific to elasmobranch taxa and detected the species present in the main tank of Lisbon Oceanarium. Field testing showed the importance of inhibitor removal prior to PCR amplification.

abstract_text: The three angelshark species living in the Mediterranean Sea, Squatina aculeata Cuvier, 1829, S. oculata Bonaparte, 1840 and S. squatina (Linnaeus, 1758), are listed as Critically Endangered Species for the basin. Alerted fishermen operating in the central and eastern Mediterranean waters provided information on the accidental capture of S. aculeata. Data on the captures of fifteen S. aculeata specimens collected between 2011 and 2018 from the Aegean and Libyan seas and from the waters of the Sicilian Channel and western Sicily are reported, adding information on the distribution and biology of this Critically Endangered elasmobranch species of the Mediterranean Sea. Data on sex, weight, depth of captures, fishing gears and the vessel names are given.

abstract_text: In this study, one female specimen of Angelshark (Squatina squatina) was incidentally caught by a commercial fisherman at a depth of 13 m on 10 May 2019 from Kabatepe Coast (North Aegean Sea, Turkey). The specimen was measured with a caliper and a precision scale in order to obtain morphometric and meristic characters including, total length, standard length, caudal length, gills opening, pre-first dorsal length, pre second dorsal length, pelvic to caudal space, eye diameter, pectoral origin, anal origin, Outer nostils, nostils between inner commers, mouth length, mouth width, first dorsal fin length, second dorsal fin length. Additionally, digestive tract and stomach content of the angelshark was examined under a loop and a stereomicroscope (Olympus, SD30 only when needed). Morphometric and meristic characters of the captured specimen are compared with the other Mediterranean records. According to our examination, upper and lower beaks of the cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis), Seranus scriba as a whole were identified. Moreover, leaves of Posidonia oceanica, Zostera marina associated with macro plastic litter (a part of plastic bag) were found in the stomach content. Detection of the macro plastic litter part in the stomach of the Angelfish is firstly recorded with this study.
